cable-cross-y-raise-lying-or-standing.name: Cable cross Y raise (lying or standing)
cable-cross-y-raise-lying-or-standing.summary: Cable lateral raise in a Y path for side delts, with tension where dumbbells give none at the bottom.
setup: Coach's setup: lie on the floor between a close-set pair of pulleys, cams about 3 pin holes above chest height.
Bench option: keep the cams the same distance in front of your sternum and use a low-to-moderate incline.
Cross the cables: each hand takes the handle from the opposite side.
cues: Start super slow – the bottom 3 inches is where the money is.
Think OUT, not up; sweep wide into a Y.
Carry the rep smoothly through to the end range.
Shoulders stay down – no shrugging.
Lower under control back to the start.
mistakes: Load so heavy you have to shrug to move it.
Rushing the start of the rep.
Lifting up toward the ears instead of out.

incline-plate-loaded-press.name: Incline plate-loaded press
incline-plate-loaded-press.summary: Main upper-chest press of the push day; the machine path lets you push hard safely near failure.
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Feet flat, upper back tight, shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Grip just wider than shoulders, wrists stacked over elbows.
cues: Lower under control to a deep, comfortable stretch.
Keep the chest up and shoulders pinned back.
Drive up and slightly in; elbows about 45–60° from your body.
Stop just short of lockout to keep tension on the chest.
mistakes: Seat too high – handles end up at the neck or shoulders.
Shoulders rolling forward at the top.
Bouncing out of the bottom.

flat-plate-loaded-press.name: Flat plate-loaded press
flat-plate-loaded-press.summary: Mid/lower chest compound press for overall chest mass and pressing strength.
setup: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest.
Feet flat, shoulder blades back and down, slight arch.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders.
cues: Lower slowly into a full chest stretch.
Keep shoulder blades pinned throughout.
Press through the palms, elbows about 45–60°.
Squeeze the chest; don't slam into lockout.
mistakes: Shoulders shrugging or rolling forward.
Cutting depth short as the set gets hard.
Elbows flared straight out at 90°.

lateral-raise-machine.name: Lateral raise machine
lateral-raise-machine.summary: Isolates the side delts for shoulder width with steady machine tension.
setup: Set the seat so the shoulder joint lines up with the machine's pivot.
Pads rest on the outside of the forearms/elbows.
Sit tall, chest against the pad if there is one.
cues: Lead with the elbows, out to the sides.
Raise to about shoulder height.
Keep shoulders down, neck relaxed.
Lower slowly; don't let the stack touch between reps.
mistakes: Shrugging the weight up with the traps.
Pivot misaligned with the shoulder.
Swinging the torso.

cable-triceps-pressdown.name: Cable triceps pressdown
cable-triceps-pressdown.summary: Simple, heavy-ish triceps isolation that is easy to progress.
setup: Attach a bar or rope to a high pulley.
Stand close, slight forward lean, elbows at your sides.
cues: Pin the elbows to your sides.
Push down until arms are fully straight; squeeze.
Let the forearms rise until just above 90°, then repeat.
Keep the shoulders down and still.
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and up.
Leaning over and pushing with body weight.
Cutting the lockout short.

cross-body-triceps-cable.name: Cross-body triceps cable
cross-body-triceps-cable.summary: Single-arm cable extension across the body to load each triceps on its own.
setup: Set a single handle at about shoulder height.
Stand side-on; reach across your body with the far arm to take it.
Upper arm roughly parallel to the floor, elbow pointing to the side.
cues: Keep the upper arm still – only the forearm moves.
Extend out across and away until the arm is straight.
Squeeze the triceps at lockout.
Return slowly until the hand is near the opposite shoulder.
mistakes: Turning it into a rear-delt fly by swinging the upper arm.
Rotating the torso to finish the rep.
Going too heavy to reach full lockout.

reverse-pec-deck.name: Reverse pec deck
reverse-pec-deck.summary: Rear-delt isolation for shoulder balance and posture alongside the pressing.
setup: Face the pad; set handles to the rear-delt position.
Seat height so the handles are at shoulder level.
Neutral or pronated grip, arms nearly straight.
cues: Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc.
Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
Stop when arms are in line with the body.
Keep shoulders down; lower slowly.
mistakes: Squeezing the shoulder blades hard so the traps take over.
Bending the elbows more as you fatigue.
Using momentum to swing the handles.

hanging-leg-raise.name: Hanging leg raise
hanging-leg-raise.summary: Core work emphasizing pelvic control and the lower abs.
setup: Grip just outside shoulder width.
Dead hang: hands are hooks, arms are ropes.
Pull the shoulder blades down and lock them there.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under ("scared dog") before lifting.
Keep legs straight and lift them OUT, as far from you as possible – don't think "up".
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Don't let the shoulders cave or the hips swing behind you (no "duck butt").
mistakes: Swinging and using momentum.
Losing the scap depression and hanging on the joints.
Arching the low back instead of tilting the pelvis.

lat-pulldown-medium-grip.name: Lat pulldown - medium grip
lat-pulldown-medium-grip.summary: Primary vertical pull for lat width.
setup: Set the thigh pad snug.
Grip about shoulder width or slightly wider, overhand.
Sit tall, slight lean back, chest up.
cues: Start each rep by pulling the shoulders down.
Drive the elbows down to your sides.
Bring the bar to the upper chest.
Let the arms rise fully for a lat stretch at the top.
mistakes: Leaning way back and turning it into a row.
Pulling with the hands/biceps instead of the elbows.
Partial reps without the top stretch.

sa-diagonal-pull-lat-bias.name: SA Diagonal pull - lat bias
sa-diagonal-pull-lat-bias.summary: Single-arm pull on a diagonal path that matches lat fiber direction for a big stretch and contraction.
setup: Set a single handle on a high pulley.
Stand or kneel slightly off to the side so the cable comes from high and across.
Start with the arm long and the lat stretched.
cues: Pull the elbow down and back toward your hip.
Keep the torso still; don't rotate to cheat.
Squeeze the lat at the bottom.
Return slowly into a full stretch.
mistakes: Turning the torso to finish the rep.
Pulling to the chest instead of the hip.
Short stretch at the top.

chest-supported-row-lat-bias.name: Chest-supported row - lat bias
chest-supported-row-lat-bias.summary: Row with the chest braced so the lats do the work without low-back fatigue.
setup: Set the chest pad so you reach the handles with arms fully extended.
Neutral grip if available, chest firmly on the pad.
cues: Keep elbows close to your sides.
Pull the elbows back toward your hips, not your armpits.
Chest stays on the pad the whole rep.
Reach forward fully for the stretch.
mistakes: Flaring elbows wide (shifts work to upper back).
Lifting the chest off the pad to heave.
Shrugging at the end of the rep.

machine-row-for-rear-delts.name: Machine row for rear delts
machine-row-for-rear-delts.summary: Wide-elbow row that biases the rear delts and upper back.
setup: Set the seat so the handles are about chest/shoulder height.
Overhand grip, wider than shoulders.
cues: Flare the elbows out wide, about shoulder height.
Pull with the elbows, not the hands.
Stop when the elbows are in line with your torso.
Keep shoulder blades fairly relaxed; feel the rear delts.
mistakes: Over-rowing so the shoulder blades and traps take over.
Dropping the elbows into a normal row.
Going too heavy and jerking.

preacher-curl-machine.name: Preacher curl machine
preacher-curl-machine.summary: Biceps isolation with the arm braced so you can't cheat.
setup: Set the seat so armpits sit snug at the top of the pad.
Elbows lined up with the machine's pivot.
cues: Curl up and squeeze the biceps.
Lower slowly to almost full extension.
Keep upper arms glued to the pad.
Don't let the weight crash at the bottom.
mistakes: Lifting the elbows or shoulders off the pad.
Skipping the bottom half of the rep.
Elbows misaligned with the pivot.

leg-extension.name: Leg extension
leg-extension.summary: Quad isolation; a good warm-up for the knees and quads before heavier leg work.
setup: Line your knee up with the machine's pivot.
Ankle pad just above the feet.
Hold the handles and sit back firmly.
cues: Extend fully and squeeze the quads at the top.
Lower slowly under control.
Keep hips down on the seat.
Toes neutral, not pointed.
mistakes: Kicking the weight up with momentum.
Hips lifting off the seat.
Knee out of line with the pivot.

calf-raise.name: Calf raise
calf-raise.summary: Direct calf work using a full range of motion.
setup: Balls of the feet on the edge of the platform.
Knees straight but not locked.
Set the shoulder pads (or bar) so you start in a stretch.
cues: Sink into a deep stretch and pause 1–2 s.
Press up through the big toe as high as you can.
Hold the top briefly.
No bouncing.
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom.
Half reps.
Bending the knees to push the weight.

leg-press.name: Leg press
leg-press.summary: Main compound leg movement of the program.
setup: Back and hips flat on the pad.
Feet about shoulder width, mid-platform.
Release the safeties once in position.
cues: Lower until knees are deep but the low back stays on the pad.
Knees track over the toes.
Press through the whole foot.
Don't lock the knees at the top.
mistakes: Hips rolling up off the pad at the bottom.
Knees caving in.
Locking out the knees hard.

hamstring-curls.name: Hamstring curls
hamstring-curls.summary: Hamstring isolation to train knee flexion directly.
setup: Knee lined up with the machine's pivot.
Pad just above the heels.
Seated: thigh pad locked down snug. Lying: hips pressed into the bench.
cues: Curl the heels toward the glutes.
Squeeze for a moment at full contraction.
Lower slowly to almost straight.
Hips stay down.
mistakes: Hips lifting to cheat the weight up.
Dropping the weight on the way down.
Short range of motion.

romanian-deadlift-rdl.name: Romanian deadlift (RDL)
romanian-deadlift-rdl.summary: Hip-hinge that loads the hamstrings in a long stretch.
setup: Stand hip width, slight knee bend.
Bar or dumbbells close against the thighs.
Brace the core, chest proud.
cues: Push the hips back; the bar slides down the legs.
Keep the back flat and the bar close.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive the hips forward to stand; squeeze glutes.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back.
Bending the knees into a squat.
Letting the bar drift away from the legs.

planks.name: Planks
planks.summary: Core stability hold to finish the leg day.
setup: Forearms under shoulders.
Legs straight, feet about hip width.
cues: Straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze glutes and brace the abs.
Tuck the pelvis slightly.
Breathe steadily.
mistakes: Hips sagging.
Hips piked high.
Holding your breath.

sa-lateral-raise-cable-knee-height.name: SA lateral raise - cable (knee height)
sa-lateral-raise-cable-knee-height.summary: Single-arm cable lateral raise with the pulley at knee height for tension through the whole range.
setup: Set the pulley at about knee height.
Stand side-on; take the handle with the far hand.
Hold the machine with the other hand for support.
cues: Raise out to the side, leading with the elbow.
Stop around shoulder height.
Keep shoulder down, neck relaxed.
Lower slowly across the body.
mistakes: Shrugging up.
Leaning the torso away to cheat.
Bending the elbow more as reps get hard.

sa-triceps-ext-straight-from-shoulder.name: SA triceps ext straight from shoulder
sa-triceps-ext-straight-from-shoulder.summary: Single-arm cable triceps extension with the upper arm out in front for a stretched-position triceps load.
setup: Set a single handle at about shoulder height.
Face away from the stack; upper arm points straight forward from the shoulder.
Elbow bent, hand near the side of the head.
cues: Keep the upper arm still.
Extend forward until the arm is straight.
Squeeze the triceps at lockout.
Return slowly into a full bend.
mistakes: Letting the elbow drop or drift.
Turning it into a press with the shoulder.
Cutting the stretch short.

lat-pulldown-neutral-grip.name: Lat pulldown - neutral grip
lat-pulldown-neutral-grip.summary: Vertical pull with a neutral grip, often allowing a stronger pull and deeper lat stretch.
setup: Attach a neutral-grip handle.
Thigh pad snug, sit tall, slight lean back.
cues: Pull the shoulders down first.
Drive the elbows down and in toward your sides.
Bring the handle to the upper chest.
Let it rise fully for the stretch.
mistakes: Leaning way back and rowing.
Pulling with the arms only.
Skipping the top stretch.

seated-row-upper-back-bias.name: Seated row - upper-back bias
seated-row-upper-back-bias.summary: Horizontal row with the elbows higher and wider to bias the upper back.
setup: Wide grip or wide handle.
Feet on the platform, knees soft, sit tall.
cues: Pull toward the lower chest with elbows out at about 45–60°.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end.
Keep the torso upright – no rocking.
Reach forward and let the shoulder blades spread.
mistakes: Rocking the torso to move the weight.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
Tucking elbows in (turns it into a lat row).

rear-delt-cable-fly-bilateral.name: Rear delt cable fly bilateral
rear-delt-cable-fly-bilateral.summary: Two-arm cable rear-delt fly for constant tension on the rear delts.
setup: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height.
Cross the cables: left hand takes the right cable, right hand the left.
Step back to center, arms out in front.
cues: Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows.
Stop when arms are in line with the body.
Return slowly until the hands cross.
mistakes: Shrugging or squeezing the traps.
Pulling with bent arms like a row.
Leaning back to cheat.

cable-rope-hammer-drag-curl.name: Cable rope hammer drag curl
cable-rope-hammer-drag-curl.summary: Neutral-grip drag curl to build the brachialis and forearms with the elbows moving back.
setup: Rope on a low pulley; stand close to the stack.
Neutral grip, palms facing each other.
cues: Drag the rope up close to your body.
Let the elbows travel back as you curl.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly along the same path.
mistakes: Swinging the torso.
Letting the rope drift away from the body.
Elbows pushing forward (turns into a normal curl).

bicep-curl-machine.name: Bicep curl machine
bicep-curl-machine.summary: Strict biceps isolation with a fixed path.
setup: Set the seat so the upper arms lie flat on the pad.
Elbows lined up with the machine's pivot.
cues: Curl up and squeeze hard at the top.
Lower slowly to nearly straight.
Keep shoulders down and back.
Upper arms stay on the pad.
mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad.
Rushing the lowering phase.
Partial reps at the top only.

warmup-band-resisted-90-degree-internal-.name: Band resisted 90 degree internal/external rotation
warmup-band-resisted-90-degree-internal-.summary: Rotator cuff warm-up through internal and external rotation in the 90/90 position.
setup: Anchor a light band at shoulder height.
Upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Face the anchor for external rotation; turn away for internal rotation.
cues: Rotate around the elbow – the upper arm stays still.
Move slow and controlled.
Keep the shoulder down, not shrugged.
Light band; it's a warm-up.
mistakes: Letting the elbow drop below shoulder height.
Using a band that's too heavy.
Arching the back to finish the rotation.

warmup-external-rotation-at-90-by-itself.name: External rotation at 90° (by itself)
warmup-external-rotation-at-90-by-itself.summary: Isolated external rotation at 90° to prep the rotator cuff for pressing.
setup: Upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Start with the forearm pointing forward/down.
cues: Rotate the forearm up until vertical.
Keep the elbow fixed at shoulder height.
Slow and controlled both ways.
Shoulder stays down.
mistakes: Elbow sagging.
Going too heavy.
Leaning back to get extra range.

warmup-serratus-wall-walks.name: Serratus wall walks
warmup-serratus-wall-walks.summary: Serratus activation drill to set up healthy shoulder-blade movement before upper-body work.
setup: Face a wall with forearms on it, about shoulder width.
Optional: light mini-band around the wrists.
cues: Push the forearms into the wall and spread the shoulder blades.
Walk the arms up the wall one at a time.
Keep pushing into the wall the whole way.
Walk back down under control.
mistakes: Arching the low back.
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears.
Losing pressure against the wall.

warmup-bent-over-i-s-y-s-and-t-s.name: Bent over I's, Y's, and T's
warmup-bent-over-i-s-y-s-and-t-s.summary: Scapular warm-up that hits the upper back and shoulder stabilizers in three positions.
setup: Hinge forward to about 45° or more, flat back.
Arms hang down, thumbs up.
cues: I: raise arms straight overhead in line with the body.
Y: raise arms up and out in a Y.
T: raise arms straight out to the sides.
Move slowly, shoulders down, brief hold at the top.
mistakes: Shrugging instead of using the shoulder blades.
Rounding the back.
Using weights that cause swinging.
